answer:
**Top 4 interstate wars (1800‑2011)** – *combatant‑only death tolls*  
(Our World in Data, Project Mars – “Wars ranked by death toll, 1800‑2011”)

| Rank | War | Approx. combatant deaths |
|------|--------------------------------------|---------------------------|
| 1 | **World War II** | ≈ 21.1 million |
| 2 | **World War I** | ≈ 7.11 million |
| 3 | **Second Sino‑Japanese War** (1937‑1945) | ≈ 1.69 million |
| 4 | **Chinese Civil War** (1927‑1950) | ≈ 1.20 million |

**Source**  
Our World in Data – “Wars ranked by death toll, 1800‑2011” (combatant deaths only).  
Link: <https://ourworldindata.org/grapher/deaths‑in‑wars‑by‑war‑1800-2011-bar‑chart>  

These figures are taken directly from the bar‑chart data set, which lists each conventional interstate conflict between 1800 and 2011 with its estimated number of combatant casualties. The four wars shown above are the highest‑ranking entries for that period.
